scope: pkg/magelib/terminology.go (CheckTerminology skip parsing), pkg/magelib/filelength.go (CheckFileLength skip parsing)
violation: Both shared gates can be silently disabled by a plausible configuration value, and the two defects are one defect at two sites: the skip-parsing logic is duplicated between CheckTerminology and CheckFileLength, and it has already drifted. (1) CheckTerminology's bare-name skip branch is unvalidated. Its PATH branch validates properly and carries the correct reasoning verbatim - 'A skip that silently matches nothing, or silently matches everything, is worse than no skip at all: the gate goes quiet and quiet is indistinguishable from clean' - and rejects '.', '..' and absolute paths. One else-branch away, a bare name is taken as `skipNames[n] = true` with no checks. WalkDir's root entry is named '.', so `CheckTerminology(rules, ".")` prunes the entire tree and returns nil. Measured 2026-08-01 against a tree containing the forbidden phrase: with no skip the gate catches it; with a bare '.' skip it reports clean. CheckFileLength guards exactly this case, because the agent building it noticed the hole while copying the pattern - so the ecosystem's newest gate is safe and its oldest is not. (2) CheckFileLength accepts any path as a skip without justification. It rejects a path claimed as BOTH waiver and skip, but a path claimed only as a skip passes unquestioned, and nothing in the mechanism distinguishes generated code the rule exempts from hand-written code someone wanted to stop hearing about. Demonstrated 2026-08-01: moving goblin's 1200-line supervisor.go from its waiver list to its skip list leaves the gate green and silent about the file. A waiver is debt that must shrink; a skip is permanent. Reclassifying the first as the second is undetectable, and a reviewer sees only a line moved between two string slices. gapi's skip has an external alibi in gopy's non-standard header; the next skip added anywhere may not.
rule: go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate; fail loudly at boundaries); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (shared mechanisms are the contract - a gate the ecosystem depends on must not be disableable by its own configuration)
exit: Close on a GATE, and on ONE parser rather than two agreeing parsers. The root cause is duplication: each gate re-implements skip parsing, they have already drifted, and a third gate would repeat the choice. Extract a single validated skip primitive that every gate consumes, so a skip that cannot mean what the caller intended is rejected once, for all of them, and correctness is not a property each new gate has to rediscover. Two things must then hold and both must be mechanically checked. (1) Every gate rejects a bare skip of '', '.' and '..'. The test is table-driven ACROSS the gates rather than written per gate - a per-gate test is the same duplication one level up and would have let this drift happen again. Demonstrated by removing the guard and showing the test fail, not by the guard existing. (2) A skip carries a required reason, so adding one means stating why the rule does not reach that path. That does not make a wrong reason impossible, but it makes the claim reviewable: 'gopy output, non-standard generated header' is checkable, while a bare path in a slice is not. The waiver/skip distinction only works if the classification is auditable at the point it is made. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN: a fourth gate added to magelib with its own skip handling, which is exactly how these two diverged - the newest gate is safe only because one agent happened to notice while copying. Nothing structurally prevents the next one from starting fresh, and a shared primitive is only shared while everyone uses it. Note also that requiring a reason string is a breaking API change for both consumers, so it needs a tag and a re-vendor in gapi and goblin, and their existing skip entries need reasons written for them rather than backfilled with 'legacy'.

scope: pkg/magelib/version.go (Version); the VERSION file in gapi, goblin and magelib; gapi/nix/package.nix:10; the release workflows in all three repos
violation: VERSION is documented in version.go as "the single source of version truth in the repo" and NOTHING verifies it against the tag being cut. Proven by the act of writing this: magelib v0.5.1 was tagged at 2286cf4f1 on 2026-08-02 with VERSION still reading 0.5.0, and no gate in any of the three repos reported it. THE HIDING MECHANISM IS THE PRECEDENCE ORDER ITSELF: Version() prefers GITHUB_REF_NAME when GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag, so a tag build reports the correct string and the stale file never surfaces - the rule that makes releases come out right is exactly what conceals the drift from everyone who could fix it. ONE DECLARATION, TWO READERS, DISAGREEING: gapi/nix/package.nix takes the other path, lib.fileContents ../VERSION, with no ref-name fallback. So a gapi tag cut without the bump produces a derivation NAMED FOR THE PREVIOUS RELEASE. Measured, not predicted: nix build .# on 71285440b built gapi-0.1.0-proto2e while the next tag is v0.1.0-proto2f. And it is BOTH artifacts, not just the store path: package.nix stamps core/version.GAPIVersion from that same lib.fileContents value, so the binary would report proto2e too. A consumer asking either the store path or `gapictl --version` gets the previous release's number. Consumers reading either one are misled. NOTE the blast radius is bounded and should not be overstated: Version() does os.ReadFile("VERSION") relative to the WORKING DIRECTORY, so gapi and goblin read their OWN VERSION file and never magelib's. A stale magelib VERSION misreports only magelib's own non-tag builds. THIRD OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-02 evening, goblin: v0.1.0-proto2f was tagged with VERSION stale and the tag had to be DELETED AND RE-CUT - hours after this entry was already open, and after the tag procedure had been written down specifically to prevent it. Three occurrences in four days. The first two were arguably knowledge failures; the third was not, because the knowledge was in hand and written down both times. That is the argument for BUILDING the gate rather than carrying the entry: filing an entry gates nothing, and neither does a procedure.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a declared invariant with no reader is not an invariant; non-determinism must be identified and bounded); go-project-manifesto (a release artifact must describe itself honestly)
exit: A magelib gate that compares VERSION against the tag ref and FAILS on disagreement, wired into each repo's release path and required, so it cannot be satisfied by a mechanism nobody invokes. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, not by a green run: one tag-ref run RED with VERSION deliberately left stale and one GREEN after the bump, differing only in that file - a single green proves nothing, per MAGELIB-DIV-001's closure. WRITE THE FALSIFIER FIRST: the gate must disagree with the default. A check that reads Version() rather than the VERSION FILE would pass unconditionally on a tag build, because GITHUB_REF_NAME wins the precedence - it would measure the emitter and not the property. It must read the file directly and compare to GITHUB_REF_NAME. RESIDUAL 1: this covers the tag path only. A VERSION bumped to a value nobody ever tags drifts the other way and stays invisible. AND THE MEASUREMENT ABOVE IS ITSELF ONLY AN APPROXIMATION, WHICH IS PART OF THE FINDING: a grep for lines beginning '//' treats a '//' inside a string literal as a comment and does not see /* */ blocks at all. Counting source lines in Go is a CALCULATION and not a filter, and any fix that reaches for a regex reproduces this defect in a new place. The exact answer is already available in the standard library - go/scanner with ScanComments tokenises the file and a line carrying at least one non-comment token is a source line - and go is the build library's only dependency, so it costs nothing to add.
rule: go-project-manifesto (the 500-line ceiling, stated there as what fine-grained single-purpose packages achieve 'WITHOUT CONTORTION' - the ceiling exists to serve comprehensibility, and a gate that makes deleting an explanation the cheapest way to comply produces a contortion of its own); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 7 (the shared build library is the ecosystem's build vocabulary, factored once and imported by every magefile so a fix lands once - filelength.go is enforced on three repos, so this is one change and not three)
exit: CLOSES ON A GATE THAT COUNTS SOURCE LINES, AND ON A CEILING THAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS CHOSEN. TWO PARTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THIS ENTRY EXISTS FOR. PART ONE, THE CALCULATION: CheckFileLength counts SOURCE lines using go/scanner with ScanComments - a line is a source line when it carries at least one non-comment token - rather than counting newlines. It must be REVERT-PROVED AGAINST THE TWO CASES A REGEX GETS WRONG: a file containing '//' inside a string literal, and a file containing a /* */ block comment, each asserted to be counted correctly. A fix that passes only on ordinary files has reproduced the defect it replaces. PART TWO, THE CEILING: the limit is SET FROM MEASUREMENT AGAINST A STATED CRITERION, not carried over because 500 was the old number. THE CRITERION IS OPERATOR-GIVEN AND IS THE POINT: a file should be small enough that a reader can hold it as ONE MENTAL MODEL - the same property a context window bounds for an agent. That is what the ceiling was always for; the number is a proxy for it. So the closing artifact includes a distribution of SOURCE lines across all three repos and a count of violations at each candidate limit, with the chosen number justified against that distribution IN THE CLOSURE. Operator's prior, recorded so the measurement can agree or disagree with it rather than being fitted to it: 500 and 750 both read as reasonable, 1000 reads as too long. NOTE THAT SLOC IS STRICTLY MORE PERMISSIVE THAN wc -l, so keeping 500 unchanged would QUIETLY LOOSEN every file's real budget by roughly the repo's comment density - about 30% - and that is a decision to take deliberately rather than by inheritance. THE CLOSING EVIDENCE THAT THE CHANGE DID SOMETHING is the Magefile.go waiver being REMOVED rather than retained: at 463 source lines it needs no waiver, so if the waiver survives the change, the change did not work. The gate must also still FAIL on the files that genuinely exceed on source lines, so this cannot be closed by a limit chosen high enough to make the problem disappear. AMENDED 2026-08-08, WHEN THE CEILING WAS MEASURED AND CHOSEN. OPERATOR DECISION: TWO CEILINGS, maxSourceLines=400 AND maxRawLines=1000, because one number cannot measure the criterion. The criterion is COGNITIVE LOAD - a file small enough to hold as one mental model - and source lines and reading length are different costs. Source lines bound the model, the state and control flow a reader must simulate, which comments reduce rather than add to. Raw lines bound the sitting-and-reading, which prose does add to. A SOURCE CEILING ALONE PLACES NO BOUND ON FILE LENGTH AT ALL: nothing in a 400-source rule stops a 3000-line file, so the second ceiling is a backstop rather than a duplicate. 1000 is not invented - operator decision 23 already states magefiles may grow to 1000 lines before splitting is looked at. THE MEASUREMENT, over 464 hand-written tracked .go files across all three repos, counted with the same go/scanner calculation the gate now uses: source lines median 93, p75 149, p90 221, p99 416, max 602; raw lines median 144, p90 346, p99 612, max 891; prose density median 36 percent, p25 29, p75 47. Violations by source at each candidate: 300->18, 350->10, 400->6, 450->4, 500->2, 750->0. 400 sits at p99, so it argues with the top one percent and nothing else, and 750 was excluded by this exit's own terms as a limit high enough to make the problem disappear. THE LOOSENING IS REAL AND WAS TAKEN DELIBERATELY, and this entry's earlier estimate of it was too small. A 500-line RAW ceiling was permitting about 318 source lines at the median 36 percent density - not the ~30 percent estimated above, which was read off the largest files rather than the corpus. So 400 source lines is roughly a quarter more permissive than what the old gate actually enforced, accepted because it measures the right quantity. THE CLOSING EVIDENCE MOVES REPOS, AND THE CLAUSE ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED. This exit predicted gapi's Magefile.go waiver would be REMOVED as proof the change did something, which was true at a 500 ceiling - it is 468 source lines - and is FALSE at 400. gapi's six waivers are exactly its six files over 400 source lines, so its list is unchanged. GOBLIN'S IS THE ONE THAT GOES: its sole waiver, Magefile.go, is 382 source lines and the stale-waiver rule FAILS the gate on a waiver whose file now passes, so the deletion is forced by construction rather than left to somebody remembering. That is the same evidence in a better form. PART ONE IS DONE: CheckFileLength counts source lines via go/scanner with ScanComments, revert-proved against both cases a regex gets wrong - '//' inside a string literal, and a /* */ block spanning lines - plus a raw string literal spanning lines, which counts as source. WHAT REMAINS: the consumers re-vendor and goblin deletes its now-stale waiver. This entry closes then, not before.

scope: pkg/magelib/hermetic.go:22 (baseTools) with hermeticTools and CheckHermetic; the consumer-side effect is goppydae-docs' flake.nix, which carries gcc and protobuf for tools nothing in that repo invokes
violation: THE HERMETIC CHECK'S TOOL SET CAN ONLY BE ADDED TO, NEVER STATED, SO EVERY CONSUMER INHERITS A COMPILER SET WHETHER OR NOT IT COMPILES ANYTHING. baseTools is a package-level var holding {go, gcc, protoc}. hermeticTools copies it, appends pandoc when the shell has it, then appends the caller's extras - so CheckHermetic(extra...) is additive by construction, and there is no parameter, field or option by which a repo can say it does not build C or generate protobuf. A repo whose targets are hugo, a linter and a content check must still put gcc and protoc in its devshell, or the gate that exists to prove the shell is hermetic fails on tools the shell has no reason to hold. MEASURED, AND ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THE PLACE IT COSTS: goppydae-docs' flake.nix lists gcc and protobuf under a nine-line comment saying they are there 'to satisfy the gate, not because a target runs them', and naming this var as the cause. That comment is the defect's receipt. THIS IS NOT MAGELIB-DIV-003 REOPENED, AND THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE. -003 was that the gate covered too FEW tools - buf, golangci-lint and gosec were unchecked - and it resolved by making CheckHermetic variadic so a repo could ADD. The additive form IS -003's resolution and it stays correct. What no caller can do is SUBTRACT, and -003 never asked for that because all three of its repos compile C and generate protobuf. A fourth consumer that does neither is what made the asymmetry visible. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED IN THE SAME BREATH, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A LEDGER ENTRY AND NOT A WORKAROUND: the hub could fork its own hermetic check and declare exactly what it runs, and that would be a fourth copy of a check the shared build library exists to factor once. Choosing two unused packages over a fork is the right call and it is still a cost paid every time a consumer appears. THE GATE ALSO MISSTATES ITSELF WHEN IT FIRES: a hub developer who has not read the flake gets "protoc not found. Run 'nix develop'" from a shell that IS the nix develop shell, for a tool the repo does not use - an error naming the wrong remedy, in the one situation the check exists to make legible.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (the shared build library is the ecosystem's build vocabulary, factored once and imported by every magefile so a fix lands once - a consumer that cannot express its own tool set is pushed toward the per-repo fork that rule exists to prevent); go-project-manifesto (explicit over implicit, and fail loudly at boundaries with an error that names its own cause - a hardcoded base set states its requirement nowhere and then reports it as a missing tool)
exit: CLOSES ON AN EXPORTED ENTRY POINT THAT TAKES THE WHOLE TOOL LIST, so a repo DECLARES what it runs instead of inheriting a compiler set. CheckHermetic(extra...) stays as it is - gapi and goblin vendor this package and call it with no arguments, and for a repo that does compile C and generate protobuf the additive form is right - so this ADDS a way to be explicit rather than removing a convenience. THE CLOSING ARTIFACT IS ON THE CONSUMER SIDE, NOT THIS REPO'S: gcc and protobuf come OUT of goppydae-docs' flake.nix, its nine-line comment comes out with them, and mage doctor plus mage lint stay green in that shell. If the flake still carries them after the change, the change did not work - the same test MAGELIB-DIV-014 applies to the Magefile waiver. REVERT-PROOF: with the two packages already out of the shell, restoring the additive-only call must produce "gcc not found. Run 'nix develop'" from inside the devshell. A green on the new path alone does not distinguish a working override from a check that stopped resolving anything, which is the failure mode -003's own closure had to guard against with a wrapper rather than a symlink. RIDES A MAGELIB TAG AND A RE-VENDOR, and the hub is the exception that makes it cheap: goppydae-docs resolves magelib through go.work in development and is not one of the two vendoring consumers, so the flake change can be proved locally before the tag exists. RESIDUAL THAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: DoctorConfig.SharedTools and the value handed to the hermetic check are two separate lists that a comment asks callers to keep equal, and nothing asserts it - so the doctor and the gate can still report different tool sets. scope: pkg/magelib/docsassets/hugo-base.yaml.tmpl (the pkgsite element in the sidebar menu block) and pkg/magelib/docsassets/layouts/partials/sidebar/element/pkgsite.html; DocsConfig.Repo at pkg/magelib/docs.go:99, which feeds it
violation: EVERY SITE ADVERTISES A pkg.go.dev LINK THAT IS WRONG FOR ALL FOUR REPOS TODAY AND WRONG FOR ONE OF THEM PERMANENTLY, AND NO CONSUMER CAN DECLINE IT. hugo-base.yaml.tmpl emits `- type: pkgsite / repo: "{{ .Repo }}"` unconditionally into the sidebar, and the partial renders https://pkg.go.dev/<repo>. TWO DISTINCT PROBLEMS SHARE ONE CAUSE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM EXPIRES. rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (the shared build library is the ecosystem's build vocabulary, factored once and imported by every magefile - a consumer that cannot express its own shape is pushed toward the per-repo fork that rule exists to prevent, and here the only available override is a wholesale restatement that drifts); go-project-manifesto (explicit over implicit - one config field silently deciding three unrelated links is a requirement stated nowhere)

Both halves asserted, because a change that removed it everywhere would satisfy the first and quietly break the second - the same shape MAGELIB-DIV-015's revert-proof guards against. RIDES A MAGELIB TAG AND A RE-VENDOR, and belongs with MAGELIB-DIV-012 and -013 on v0.9.0 because it is the same embedded-asset cascade. RESIDUAL THAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: DocsConfig.Repo still decides the GitHub link and the default EditURL together, so the overloading survives for the two uses that happen to agree today.
